scope: Current uncommitted codex/v0.6: optional contrast comparison, grain clock after GPU admission, stable CPU scene-input caching and prompt keyboard release. Moving static remains unresolved; exact-class reuse stays offline.

gameplay.detail: Both backends preserve comparison pose/collectibles and exact contrast mapping; key release settles by 300 ms then holds identical pixels. Fullscreen/pointer lock still require real clicks.

checks.foundationBackend: Auto prefers WebGPU; explicit CPU compatibility remains available; failure selects CPU fallback.

productionSmoke.scope: Production build contains enabled Reduce moving bands. Same current graph and depth calibration; direct GPU tone generation; fine changing grain during camera/visibility motion and a held carrier at rest. CPU compatibility passed the same 40 gameplay checks.
productionSmoke.current: Production rebuilt successfully; current gameplay checks ran against live development source, not a separate production server.

checks.preferenceMigration: Unit coverage: previous legacy saves and a changed preset signature restore current defaults; same-preset custom choices persist.

finalDiagnosticMetadata.noiseFrame: Captured current uint32 identifier; zero selects original static reference.
finalDiagnosticMetadata.carrierContrast: A=1, optional B=0.5; captured per frame

gpuFixtures.foundation: 27 dynamic carrier/frame/contrast cases (binary/white/pink, frames 1/2/uint32-max, contrasts 1/.75/.5) preserve exact roots/pairs, held frames and zero measured CPU/GPU grayscale difference. Static reference/presentation checks retained.

performanceSample.scope: Historical, not remeasured this turn. Development gameplay after QA completed; 1280x720, DPR 1, pink/96/.33, positive noiseFrame 18 held at rest, native scale 1. HUD cadence sample, not a sustained motion benchmark.
performanceSample.note: Completion includes scheduling; not a GPU timestamp.

motion.method: Image-only local correlation at horizontal shifts -12..12 and vertical -4..4; 16 current city frames, turning and forward movement, both contrasts.
motion.scope: Engineering checks, not perceived bands, comfort or sustained performance.

liveDevelopment.firefox: Direct inspection blocked by Computer Use because Firefox URL-policy enforcement is unsupported. No browser settings changed; user needs one refresh to load live client.
liveDevelopment.scope: Earlier source/HMR verification retained; server source now includes current changes. Direct Firefox inspection remains unavailable.

checks.sourceIntegrity: Hashes identify files tested at recordedAt. Later tiny-step diagnostics and center-guide UI edits are outside that run; the full gameplay suite was not rerun for these additions. Core stereo synthesis remains unchanged. Historical HMR/performance observations retain their earlier scope.

limitations: Human retains depth; dynamic carrier greatly improved moving bands, with one later suspected brief diamond band. Half contrast helps but harsh static remains. No general comfort or release acceptance.
No previous RGB/depth accumulation. Integer disparity terracing and legacy color propagation are not solved by this carrier change.
Procedural pink approximates 1/f with normalized octaves; independent spectral tests cover inputs, not arbitrary occlusion mapping.
Refresh limited to 60 Hz on camera/visibility changes; general animated hosts must supply their own noiseFrame policy.
Initial static CPU FFT and 2 MP bounds remain. FPS observation is stationary with a dynamic carrier held, not a hardware-floor or sustained-motion benchmark.
Fullscreen, captured mouse and forced GPU device loss were not rerun. Direct Firefox UI verification was blocked; live-source and WebSocket reload delivery were verified without browser control.

humanObservation.scope: Live game; exact settings/hardware not independently captured.
humanObservation.banding: Initially reported absent; during the 0.75-contrast comparison the user suspected one brief band at the diamond. Bounded acceptance, not universal absence.
humanObservation.fusion: User retained depth and objects/edges during movement.
humanObservation.remaining: Harsh TV static during movement; reported tail of 1–2 seconds after stopping. Faster key release is tested but not yet separately human-confirmed.
humanObservation.contrast75: Qualified improvement; depth held, main static remained harsh.
humanObservation.contrast50: B helps, but static is still too harsh.

contrastTrial.scope: Historical 0.75-contrast CPU rectangle fixture below; not a human failure threshold. Current optional live B uses 0.5.
contrastTrial.decision: Both human comparisons helped insufficiently. Leave A as default, B optional; stop contrast reductions. Comfort remains unresolved.

releaseFix.scope: Deterministic simulation; current CPU/GPU browser checks confirm key release settles by 300 ms and holds exact pixels afterward. Does not account for the full human-reported tail or prove moving comfort.

reuseHypothesis.scope: Synthetic exact-class reuse; no human comfort claim or game integration
reuseHypothesis.decision: Do not integrate: reduced average flicker concentrates changes in vertical strips or rare large refreshes. These proxies indicate risk; no human test performed.
